name: Vamsi Krishna Kocherla
title: 3D Perception · Robot Manipulation · Physics-Informed Simulation
subtitle: Robotics MS Student · ex-Production CV Scientist · recovering ECE undergrad
status: building autonomous drones & SLAM systems at UMN
tagline: I teach robots to see the world, touch it, and get the physics right.
bio: Started with signals and circuits, ended up teaching cameras to understand 3D space. Five years turning research into production computer vision — detection models on tractors, inference at the edge, systems that had to survive real outdoor light. That built a working intuition for what actually holds up in the physical world. Now at UMN, turning that intuition into rigorous method: how robots perceive the world in 3D, manipulate what they perceive, and simulate its physics well enough to trust the simulation.
focus: City-scale Gaussian Splatting with CLIP/DINOv2 semantics for language-queryable 3D scenes
Visual servoing & RL for contact-rich manipulation, trained in Isaac Sim
Estimating material properties (Young's Modulus, friction, density) from vision for sim-to-real transfer
Production inference at scale — Triton, KServe, Kubernetes, sub-500ms latency
